messages.text: Pulisic's bicycle kick puts USMNT in semis as Pochettino bids farewell

metadata.summary: A bicycle kick by Christian Pulisic helped the United States clinch its spot in the Concacaf Nations League semifinals in Mauricio Pochettino's final game.
metadata.content: USA 2-0 Haiti (Nov 17, 2026) Game Analysis - ESPN Skip to main content Skip to navigation Concacaf Nations League, Quarterfinals United States USA USA 2 FT Agg. 8-0 Haiti Haiti HAI 0 Christian Pulisic - 25' Julian Hall - 43' 2nd Leg - United States win 8-0 on aggregate USA v Haiti By ESPN News Services Updated: Nov 17, 2026, 10:29 pm Facebook Facebook Messenger Twitter Email Christian Pulisic 's bicycle kick for a score and another goal from teenager Julian Hall helped the United States men's national team clinch its spot in the Concacaf Nations League semifinals in Mauricio Pochettino's final game as coach. Already up 6-0 on Haiti from Saturday's first leg in Miami, the United States' place in March's final four had effectively been sealed before Tuesday's return match in Cincinnati. But Pulisic and Hall ensured Pochettino a winning end to his two years in charge before taking over Premier League giant Manchester United . A 2-0 victory at TQL Stadium sets up a semifinal with either Jamaica or rival Mexico in the semifinals in Inglewood, California. Pochettino departs with a 23-12-2 record and with the team on a six-game winning streak following its World Cup exit at the hands of Belgium . Christian Pulisic celebrates his goal in the USMNT's win over Haiti. Robin Alam/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images U.S. under-23 coach Steve Cherundolo will lead the team during December's training camp, with a permanent replacement yet to be announced. metadata.summary: The WBC will support a 2027 unification between its heavyweight champion and the winner of Tyson Fury’s vs Anthony Joshua.
metadata.content: WBC boss Mauricio Sulaiman 'absolutely' supports Agit Kabayel title unification for Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua winner | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive WBC boss Mauricio Sulaiman 'absolutely' supports Agit Kabayel title unification for Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua winner Tyson Fury meets Anthony Joshua for the WBA 'super' heavyweight title on December 11, while Agit Kabayel puts the WBC belt on the line against Nelson Hysa on November 28; WBC president Mauricio Sulaiman will "absolutely" back a unification with the Fury-AJ winner next John Dennen Sports Journalist @johndennen Wednesday 18 November 2026 06:55, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A look inside Tyson Fury's training camp ahead of his December 11 showdown with Anthony Joshua The WBC will support a 2027 unification between its heavyweight champion and the winner of Tyson Fury’s vs Anthony Joshua. Agit Kabayel will defend his WBC heavyweight title against Nelson Hysa on November 28, and if he successfully defends his belt the WBC will "absolutely" be in favour of a meeting with the winner of the huge all-British heavyweight showdown on December 11. Fury vs Joshua could have been a final eliminator for the WBC title, though Fury and Joshua will now box for the WBA 'super' heavyweight championship. messages.text: Zverev books place in ATP Finals semi-finals

metadata.summary: Alexander Zverev booked his spot in the knockout stages of the ATP Finals after sealing a ruthless 6-2 7-6 (7-4) victory over Ben Shelton in Turin on Tuesday night, in a rematch of this year's US Open final.
metadata.content: ATP Finals: Alexander Zverev books place in semi-finals after brushing aside Ben Shelton; Arthur Fils beats Rafael Jodar | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content ATP Finals: Alexander Zverev books place in semi-finals after brushing aside Ben Shelton; Arthur Fils beats Rafael Jodar Alexander Zverev beat Ben Shelton in straight sets to book his place in the knockout stages of the ATP Finals; Rafael Jodar will not progress past the groups after he suffered defeat to Arthur Fils; watch the ATP Nitto Finals live on Sky Sports Tennis Tuesday 17 November 2026 22:42, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alexander Zverev booked his spot in knockout stages of the ATP Finals with a victory against Ben Shelton Alexander Zverev booked his spot in the knockout stages of the ATP Finals after sealing a ruthless 6-2 7-6 (7-4) victory over Ben Shelton in Turin on Tuesday night, in a rematch of this year's US Open final. His victory means debutant Rafael Jodar will not advance to the semi-finals after the Spaniard suffered defeat to Zverev in their opening match of the tournament, before being bested 4-6 6-2 6-2 by Arthur Fils earlier in the day. Zverev, whose service game was impeccable against Shelton, will jump to the top of the John McEnroe Group standings, having not dropped a set so far during the tournament, as he swept away the American to bring up a flawless 7-0 winning record against the 24-year-old.
